Article Title: 'They would kick us': Stalin takes on Vijay over 'jaw gesture', recalls Emergency-era prison days
Article Text:
His remarks came after Vijay launched a strong attack on the DMK in the assembly

NEW DELHI: DMK president MK Stalin on Thursday hit back at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over his recent remarks in the state assembly, accusing him of attempting to demean the party and its leaders while recalling his arrest and alleged custodial torture during the Emergency.Responding to Vijay’s criticism of the DMK, Stalin said the party’s history and its ideological struggle could not be changed by political attacks.“Thambi Vijay, what you said is true. It is not a lie. During the Emergency, opposing it, leader Kalaignar organized a huge gathering at the Marina beach and severely criticized the MISA Act,” Stalin said in a video message shared on X.His remarks came after Vijay launched a strong attack on the DMK in the assembly on Wednesday, accusing previous governments of corruption and referring to the Sarkaria Commission as well as Enforcement Directorate documents concerning alleged corruption during the 2021-26 regime.Stalin recalled that the Union government dismissed the DMK government on January 31, 1976, during the Emergency imposed by the Indira Gandhi government.“The very next second after dismissing the government, police came to the Gopalapuram house to arrest me under the MISA Act,” Stalin said, recounting how his father and former chief minister M Karunanidhi told police that his son was away campaigning and would return the next day.Stalin said that after he returned, Karunanidhi himself called the police and asked them to arrest him.Recalling his time in prison, Stalin alleged that he was subjected to severe physical abuse and was kept with other prisoners in a small room where leprosy patients had earlier been housed.“In prison, many atrocities happened to me. We were taken and locked up in a place where leprosy patients were kept. Ten people were locked inside a small room. Inside that same room, in a single pot, all of us had to urinate,” he said.Stalin alleged that police beat prisoners with lathis at night, kicked them with boots and that other inmates also assaulted them. He recalled the death of DMK leader and former MP Chitti Babu, whom he said died in jail following the beatings.“Due to their beating, my dear brother, Member of Parliament Chitti Babu, died inside the jail itself. Due to their beating, my jawbone was broken,” Stalin said.The DMK has condemned Vijay’s remarks and announced a statewide protest on September 12, accusing the chief minister of making “scurrilous remarks” against Stalin, Karunanidhi and other party leaders.Law minister R Nirmal Kumar, however, has disputed Stalin’s account, saying there was no official record to indicate that his detention during the Emergency was under MISA. The minister said Stalin was arrested following remarks concerning Indira Gandhi and her 20-point programme.Stalin also rejected Vijay’s allegations relating to the Sarkaria Commission and corruption charges against Karunanidhi, arguing that successive governments would have acted if the allegations had been established.Turning to Vijay’s conduct in the Assembly, Stalin urged him to maintain the dignity expected of a chief minister and focus on governance rather than political controversies.“The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly has dignity and respect. It is a place sculpted by many great leaders, great men. That responsibility is now with you,” Stalin said.
Article Summary: Dmk president mk stalin hit back at tamil nadu chief minister c joseph vijay. He accused vijay of attempting to demean the party and its leaders. Stalin recalled his arrest and alleged custodial torture during the emergency. His remarks came after vijay launched a strong attack on the dmk in the assembly.

Article Title: Congress-NC rift over Vande Mataram: The ghost of 1987 and ‘big brother’ complex
Article Text:
The 1987 ghost: Vande Mataram row and why Omar Abdullah won't let Congress call the shots in J&K.

Venugopal called on allies to honour the wisdom of the freedom fighters

One alliance, two political vocabularies

The alliance and an unequal power equation

What Omar Abdullah had said in 2024

Statehood: Common demand & source of friction

The Rajya Sabha dispute

We felt that the best chance of winning that seat was with the Congress, and they felt otherwise. So be it. Omar Abdullah on RS seat deadlock

The ghost of 1987

1987: The alliance that became a warning

2009-14: History managed, but not erased

The latest Congress-National Conference (NC) clash may have begun with a song, but it is really about something much older: who gets to set the political terms of the alliance in Jammu and Kashmir?CM Omar Abdullah and NC president Farooq Abdullah stood through the full rendition of Vande Mataram on Wednesday at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar. The song was played in its complete six-stanza version, lasting about three minutes and 10 seconds, in line with the Centre's new protocol.This was in sharp contrast with the Congress's stand. Its grand-old party has reaffirmed its 1937 decision to restrict public rendition at party events to the first two stanzas, arguing that the later verses sit uneasily with the pluralist ethos of the freedom movement.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal subsequently said the full version "sits uneasily" with the syncretic and pluralist ethos envisioned by India's freedom fighters and urged allies to stand by the Congress position.The NC was quick to respond, saying the J&K government was only fulfilling its official duty. "After legislative enactment by Parliament, singing Vande Mataram and standing for the song has become a statutory obligation (mandatory legal duty) regardless of the ideological position of any party, group or alliance," said National Conference spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq.The Vande Mataram row is the latest in the list of NC-Congress differences that have surfaced post-election.However, in J&K, the dispute carries an additional historical charge.The NC has spent decades constructing its political identity around a particular proposition: New Delhi can be a partner, but it cannot be the political proprietor of Kashmir's choices.That is where the ghost of 1987 enters.The Vande Mataram dispute has once again exposed an asymmetry that has repeatedly surfaced between the two parties.Congress has to balance its position across India. For Abdullahs' NC, the principal political constituency remains rooted in J&K, where questions of identity, autonomy, federalism and the relationship with New Delhi carry a much more immediate electoral meaning.It is also why the latest row is not an isolated irritant in the alliance.In December 2025, for instance, Omar Abdullah explicitly distanced the NC from Congress's "vote chori" campaign, saying Congress was free to choose its own agenda but that it was not automatically the agenda of the INDIA bloc. With this, Omar tried to assert his party's political autonomy within the alliance.And that has been the recurring pattern.The 2024 assembly election gave the NC-Congress relationship a new lease of life, but it also made the asymmetry between the two parties stark.The alliance crossed the majority mark with 49 seats, with the NC winning 42, Congress six and CPM one. The BJP emerged with 29, PDP three and independents seven.The pre-poll negotiations themselves had not been effortless: the parties agreed that NC would contest 51 seats and Congress 32, while several constituencies remained "friendly contests".The campaign also revealed the limits of joint ownership. Congress and NC leaders did not always campaign together. In Sopore, where the two allies were in a friendly contest, Rahul Gandhi and Omar Abdullah campaigned for their respective candidates separately.During the campaign, Omar Abdullah had publicly noted that Rahul Gandhi should dedicate more campaign time and effort to the Jammu region in addition to Kashmir to maximise electoral impact.Omar himself gave the practical reason for the alliance during the campaign: it was intended to prevent a hung assembly and give voters an alternative.The alliance won the election, and the next question was: what does each side get to claim as its own?The first major post-election rupture came even before the new government had settled in.Omar Abdullah became CM in October 2024, but Congress chose to stay out of his ministry, citing restoration of statehood as its priority. While Congress backed the NC government from outside, its absence highlighted a strategic divide within the alliance. Omar had to engage with Delhi to govern the Union Territory, while Congress sought to pressure the Centre from outside. That difference in approach has repeatedly resurfaced.In July 2025, Congress announced protests in Jammu, Srinagar and Delhi and Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to PM Narendra Modi seeking legislation to restore J&K's statehood. The NC leadership was irritated because the announcement had not been coordinated with the ruling party. Some NC leaders described Congress's campaign as counterproductive and even as "sabotage" of the government's own efforts.Omar's objection was that Congress had launched the campaign without informing or consulting the NC, leaving its alliance partner caught off guard.The difference is clearer on Article 370 . The NC's 2024 manifesto explicitly called for the restoration of Articles 370 and 35A and reversal of the changes made after August 2019. Congress has similarly opposed the 2019 constitutional changes, but in its recent campaigns placed greater emphasis on the restoration of statehood.Omar reiterated in the J&K assembly in February that his government remained committed to restoring special status, even as statehood remained an immediate demand. By July 2026, he was also linking the restoration of statehood to any future discussion on J&K's earlier constitutional position.This has given the two parties different political priorities.In October 2025, the disagreement moved from ideology to seats. J&K was electing four Rajya Sabha members. The NC, which had emerged as the dominant party in the assembly, initially discussed leaving one seat for Congress.Talks failed.The NC eventually fielded candidates for all four seats after Congress decided not to contest the fourth seat it had been offered, arguing that it was not among the "safe seats" it had sought.Omar's response was strikingly matter-of-fact: "So be it."The NC-Congress disagreement ultimately cost the alliance a clean sweep, with the BJP winning the fourth seat Congress had declined to contest.To understand why the NC may be particularly sensitive to questions of control, one has to go back not merely to 1987 but to 1984.Farooq Abdullah's government was dismissed on July 2, 1984, after 12 NC legislators defected. Ghulam Mohammad Shah, Farooq's brother-in-law and leader of the defecting group, formed the government with Congress support. Contemporary accounts described the episode as a central-government intervention in Kashmir politics; Farooq called the dismissal unconstitutional.For the NC, this was not an abstract constitutional episode. It was a direct lesson in the vulnerability of a regional government to New Delhi's political machinery.Then came 1986.Rajiv Gandhi and Farooq Abdullah reached an agreement that brought the two parties together electorally. A Human Rights Watch report noted that the accord deepened a sense of betrayal among many Kashmiris, who saw Farooq Abdullah compromising with the same Congress party that had pushed him out of office two years earlier.The NC-Congress alliance won 66 of J&K's 76 assembly seats in 1987. But the result was overshadowed by the emergence of the Muslim United Front as an opposition platform, arrests of its candidates and workers, and widespread allegations of electoral rigging. Human Rights Watch later described the election as a turning point that contributed to widespread disillusionment with electoral politics.The significance of 1987 for the NC, therefore, is about the political memory it created. A generation of Kashmiri activists came to believe that the democratic route had been closed to them, a perception that became part of the backdrop to the insurgency that followed.The episode also left an enduring paradox. Congress was simultaneously the NC's electoral partner and a major force at the Centre. That history helps explain the NC's instinct to work with Congress while resisting any perception that Delhi is dictating its regional agenda.That distrust predates the 1980s. In 1953, Sheikh Abdullah was dismissed and arrested after his relationship with the Union government deteriorated. The circumstances were very different, but the political memory was similar: central intervention could reshape J&K's politics. For the NC, unlike many other regional parties, Congress's centralising past is therefore not distant history but part of its own political inheritance.The two parties showed they could overcome that history after the 2008 assembly election. The NC won 28 seats and Congress 17, and the parties formed a coalition government with Omar Abdullah as CM in 2009.But the partnership remained contested. Differences over AFSPA, administrative issues and governance repeatedly surfaced. In 2011, Congress called for consensus on AFSPA while Omar maintained that the state government was an important stakeholder.By 2014, the alliance had run its course and Congress chose to contest the assembly election separately. NC leaders argued that the association with a centrist national party had diluted the party's pro-Valley credentials, with one senior NC leader calling Congress a "very bad alliance partner".The 1987 ghost & real test of allianceWhile 1987 may still shape the NC's political instincts, it would be too simplistic to link every present-day disagreement to that history. The political and constitutional context has changed; however, the experience remains part of the backdrop to the relationship.The lesson for the NC, as we saw in the last election, has not been to avoid Congress, but to work with it where interests converge while retaining its own political space.The Vande Mataram dispute, therefore, is less significant in itself than what it reveals about continuing differences over statehood, Article 370, seat-sharing and the balance between Congress's national strategy and the NC's regional politics.The alliance can survive such differences, but the interesting question now is how durable it will be, which willdepend on how well the two parties manage their competing political priorities.
Article Summary: The latest congress-national conference clash may have begun with a song, but it is really about something much older: who gets to set the political terms of the alliance in jammu and kashmir?cm omar abdullah and nc president farooq abdullah stood through the full rendition of vande mataram on wednesday.

Article Title: 'I didn't see any benefits': Congress leader P Chidambaram questions 2026 Brics Summit
Article Text:
Chidambaram's remarks came as authorities in the capital intensified preparations for the Brics summit.

Delhi steps up preparations

Officials inspect key routes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP P Chidambaram has questioned what India has gained from recent Brics meetings, saying he has not seen any tangible benefits from the last two or three summits.With India set to host the Brics Summit 2026 in Delhi, Chidambaram said the country is part of several major international groupings but questioned whether they had delivered concrete gains for India.“I don't know how many Presidents and how many Prime Ministers are coming. I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results,” Chidambaram told news agency ANI.“In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics Summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.Chidambaram's remarks came as authorities in the capital intensified preparations for the summit. Delhi Municipal Corporation Commissioner Sanjeev Khirwar and PWD Principal Secretary Sandeep Kumar inspected key areas on Wednesday, including the summit venue and locations around Bharat Mandapam.Senior officials from both departments, including deputy commissioners from the concerned zones, accompanied them during the inspection.Khirwar reviewed sanitation and civic arrangements and directed officials to coordinate closely on cleanliness and other essential services.Officials were asked to carry out intensive cleaning and maintenance along summit routes, venues, adjoining areas, markets, roads, footpaths, green belts and other sensitive locations.The inspection also covered movement corridors in southeast Delhi, including Sarai Kale Khan, Lodhi Road and Nizamuddin, as well as Saket and Sheikh Sarai in south Delhi.Authorities were directed to deploy sufficient sanitation workers, machinery and supervisory staff during the final stage of preparations.Khirwar also called for visible improvements in enforcement, animal control, vector control, beautification, lighting and branding at identified locations.India is taking over the Brics chairship for the fourth time in 2026. The chairship is being guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, with a stated focus on a people-centric and humanity-first approach.
Article Summary: Senior congress leader and rajya sabha mp p chidambaram has questioned what india has gained from recent brics meetings. He said he has not seen any tangible benefits from the last two or three summits. Delhi steps up preparations for the brics summit.

Article Title: 'Wonder if I should become a cockroach': Vijay Mallya cries 'injustice' over bank dues
Article Text:
Vijay Mallya was declared Fugitive Economic Offenders under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018.

Mallya questions his ‘fugitive’ tag

Mentions Rs 14,131.60 crore recovery

The 'fugitive' tag

NEW DELHI: Vijay Mallya , declared a fugitive by the government, quipped on X about "becoming a cockroach", wondering if he may have a "better life on the cockroach side" as he cried "injustice" over legal action linked to his bank dues.Mallya, who is living in London, made the remarks while responding to the legal proceedings against him and defending his position on the recovery of money owed to banks by his now-defunct Kingfisher Airlines "With all the injustices I have faced and continue to face, I wonder if I should become a cockroach. Maybe a better life on the cockroach side," he wrote on X.He cited an Enforcement Directorate (ED) affidavit that he claimed was filed before the Bombay high court and alleged that the agency had confirmed the recovery of more than Rs 14,000 crore and its transfer to banks."And may I say again, affidavit filed in court by the most feared criminal agency the Enforcement Directorate confirms that they handed over Rs 14,000 plus crores to the Banks in 2021. Forget what I say if you don’t trust me. Focus on what the Enforcement Directorate said," he alleged.Mallya also argued that repayment of bank dues should not depend on his physical presence in India."Thank you all for your mixed replies to my tweets. Love and hate go hand in hand and I respectfully accept that whilst humbly accepting your opinions.But for those who do not understand the difference between permanent residency and citizenship and for those who think that repayments are based on physical presence, please think again," he claimed.A day earlier, he had said he was legally unable to leave the UK, where he claimed to have been a permanent resident since 1992."For all who say I am a bhagoda refusing to come to India, please be aware that I have been a permanent resident of the United Kingdom since 1992 and am currently legally prohibited from leaving this country. All this started with poster boy actions by the Government of India who have been grossly unjust in my case," he said in the post on X.Mallya posted what he described as an extract from an ED affidavit filed before the Bombay high court and pointed to the figure of Rs 14,131.60 crore."Affidavit filed by the ED in the Hon’ble Bombay high court. Para 7 is the decreed debt and Para 17 shows recovered Rs 14,131.60 crore in 2021 !! 5 years on I am still referred to as a fraud who cheated the Banks," he said.He also shared a table that he claimed showed the recovery made in his case and questioned why he continued to be described as a fraudster."To all who believe in fair and proper accounting justice please see the following table. Do I still deserve the way I am berated by the media and referred to as a fraudster at the very outset of a journalist’s script ? Why not start asking when I will get my refund," he said.Mallya was among 15 people declared Fugitive Economic Offenders under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018, according to a statement made by MoS Finance Pankaj Chaudhary in the Lok Sabha in October 2025. The list also included Nirav Modi.In February this year, the Bombay high court criticised Mallya and said he could not seek equitable relief while deliberately avoiding court proceedings. The court gave him a final opportunity to clarify whether he intended to return to India.Mallya's petition challenges the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act and his declaration as a fugitive economic offender.
Article Summary: Vijay mallya made the remarks while responding to the legal proceedings against him and defending his position on the recovery of money owed to banks by his now-defunct kingfisher airlines. Article Title: J&K launches 3-year rehab scheme for drug addicts
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: J&K chief secretary Atal Dulloo Wednesday rolled out a three-year scheme to rehabilitate drug addicts under treatment at govt-run or aided de-addiction centres and institutions, prevent relapse, and aid their reintegration into society.The scheme will initially be introduced in the districts of Jammu, Srinagar, Kathua and Budgam and later extended to others, officials said.Under the scheme, a structured rehabilitation cycle will be established for drug abusers to ensure a seamless transition from “detoxification to socio-economic stabilisation” to reduce relapse rates and prevent premature exit from treatment, Dulloo said.The first six months will cover intake, assessment, treatment, stabilisation and rehabilitation planning under Phase I. The next six to 24 months will involve reintegration and livelihood activation under Phase II. The following 24-36 months will revolve around sustained monitoring and social inclusion.J&K home department will facilitate tracing and support for individuals requiring intervention. The health and medical education department will provide continuing mental health services, counselling, psychiatric care, de-addiction treatment and relapse-prevention support.The education department will aid educational reintegration, academic continuity, re-enrolment, bridge learning and access to student support services, officials said.The labour and employment department will facilitate vocational training, skill development, employment placement and entrepreneurship development. The rural development and Panchayati Raj department will support community participation, family engagement, livelihood inclusion, social support networks and local-level rehabilitation and reintegration initiatives. The social welfare department will serve as the nodal department for implementation of the policy, officials said.On April 11, 2026, J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha launched a 100-day anti-drug campaign under the “Nasha Mukt Abhiyaan”, which involved large-scale awareness programmes by the civil administration and police, destruction of poppy cultivation, random urine testing of drivers and intensified crackdowns on drug networks.Over 32,500 drug abuse cases have been registered across J&K since 2022, with the highest number of patients reported from Srinagar and Jammu districts, govt data revealed. A 2022 study by Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences Kashmir estimated about 67,468 people in 10 Kashmir districts as “substance-dependent”.
Article Summary: The scheme will initially be introduced in the districts of jammu, srinagar, kathua and budgam. The first six months will cover intake, assessment, treatment, stabilisation and rehabilitation planning. The next six to 24 months will involve reintegration and livelihood activation.

Article Title: Human rights organisations condemn 'racist murder' of Manipuri singer Chongtham Vikram in Delhi
Article Text:
The groups called for support, protection and compensation for Vikram's family and urged authorities to protect them from intimidation, harassment or further victimisation.

NEW DELHI: A group of civil society and human rights organisations has condemned the death of Manipuri music teacher and singer Chongtham Vikram, who was allegedly killed by a mob in Delhi on Monday. The group called for a thorough probe into the possible racial motive behind the attack.The joint statement was issued after a meeting of the Manipur Students’ Association Delhi (MSAD), Manipur International Youth Centre (MIYC), People’s Progressive Alliance Manipur (PPAM), Karwan-e-Mohabbat (KeM), North East India Support Centre and Helpline (NEISCH) and Human Rights Alert (HRA) on September 8 at the Centre for Equity Studies in Sarvodaya Enclave, New Delhi.The groups said Vikram's murder should not be treated as an isolated criminal incident. They said it must be examined in the wider context of racial prejudice and violence faced by people from Northeast India.The statement said an FIR, numbered 0296, has been registered at Sunlight Colony police station under Sections 103(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.Section 103(2) deals with murder committed by a group of five or more people acting together on grounds including race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language or personal belief.Section 3(5) provides for joint liability when several people commit a criminal act in furtherance of a common intention.The organisations said the police investigation so far appeared inadequate to address what they described as a broader pattern of racist crimes against people from the Northeast.They also pointed to the recommendations of the MP Bezbaruah Committee, which was set up by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and submitted its report in 2014. The committee had recommended measures to tackle discrimination, violence and the vulnerabilities faced by people from Northeast India.The groups said most of those recommendations, including a proposal to specifically criminalise racist acts, remain unimplemented.They also highlighted the absence of a comprehensive legal framework dealing specifically with racial discrimination. The statement noted that Article 15 of the Constitution prohibits discrimination on several grounds but does not expressly list colour, descent, national origin or ethnic origin.The organisations further cited recommendations issued by the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) on August 25, 2026. They urged the Centre to adopt comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation with a clear definition of racial discrimination, covering both direct and intersecting forms of discrimination in public and private spheres.The groups demanded an impartial and transparent investigation into Vikram's death, including an evidence-based examination of any racial motive.They also called for all those responsible to be identified and prosecuted, including anyone who may have participated in, facilitated or encouraged the attack.The organisations urged authorities to ensure that the case is not investigated merely as an ordinary criminal offence without considering its alleged racial dimensions.They also sought immediate measures to prevent further racist violence against people from Northeast India, along with institutional mechanisms to tackle racial discrimination and hate-based violence.The groups called for support, protection and compensation for Vikram's family and urged authorities to protect them from intimidation, harassment or further victimisation.The statement said, "Justice for Chongtham Vikram is not merely a demand for accountability for one murder. It is a demand for dignity, equality, security, and the fundamental right to live free from racial violence for all people from Northeast India."The meeting ended with a two-minute silence in memory of Vikram and in solidarity with his bereaved family.
Article Summary: Chongtham vikram was allegedly killed by a mob in delhi on monday. The group called for a thorough probe into the possible racial motive behind the attack. They said it must be examined in the wider context of racial prejudice and violence faced by people from northeast india.

Article Title: Can husband be tried for marital rape if law says not offence: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Centre should go back to drawing board if law has a problem, says SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Citing Article 20(1) of the Constitution which shields persons from prosecution for an act which is not an offence under existing penal laws, the Supreme Court on Wednesday asked whether a husband can be prosecuted for marital rape when the law categorically states that it is not an offence, even as it agreed with the Centre that the matter should be left for Parliament’s consideration.Article 20(1) provides that “no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of law in force at that time…” Section 375(2) of IPC said “sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being under 15 years, is not rape” (wife’s age was raised to 18 by SC in 2017), with the provision replicated in Sect 63(2) of BNS.With a bunch of petitions challenging the constitutional validity of this exception to rape, a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the matter posed foundational questions, especially citing the case in which a husband has challenged a Karnataka high court decision to permit his prosecution for marital rape.The hearing saw Solicitor General Tushar Mehta arguing that the issue, given its complexity, be left for the Parliament to consider.It will be absurd for courts to take upon themselves the task of determining the nature of sex — natural or unnatural — when it is best left to people, their representatives and legislature, SG Tushar Mehta said.The bench agreed. “It should always come from Parliament. If the govt feels there is a problem with the law, then it should go back to the drawing board and recast the law with approval of Parliament,” it said.During the last hearing, SC had wondered whether the court can rewrite penal laws to create a new offence.Senior advocate Karuna Nundy said that no new offence needs to be created as the offence of rape is already defined and the only question is whether it is constitutionally justified to grant immunity from it to a class of persons (husbands).
Article Summary: Centre should go back to drawing board if law has a problem, says sc. Article 20(1) provides that “no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of law in force at that time…” section 375(2) of ipc said “sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being under 15 years, is not rape”

Article Title: NC tells Congress: Full Vande Mataram a constitutional duty
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: National Conference fired a political broadside at ally Congress Wednesday, defending full renditions of Vande Mataram at govt functions in J&K as a “constitutional” duty.Congress objected after all six stanzas of the national song was played at the inauguration of J&K’s first international film festival in Srinagar attended by CM Omar Abdullah and NC president Farooq Abdullah on Sept 7. As at other official functions, Omar stood at attention throughout.J&K Congress president Tariq Hamid Karra said NC and Congress should respect how the song’s place in India’s national life evolved through both the freedom movement and constitutional journey. “National symbols, songs and traditions occupy a special place in the heart of every Indian. Their true strength lies in their ability to bind together a nation as diverse as ours,” he said, calling it a concern that alliance partners had chosen to sing the full version.NC countered, asking Congress to look at CMs of states governed by the party, including Telangana and Karnataka, who have participated in full renditions.NC chief spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq shared on X a video featuring Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar at an event where the unabridged song was sung. He said govt protocol must be separated from party ideology. “NC has a clear stand. When Parliament has adopted it, playing Vande Mataram becomes a statutory obligation and that is what govt did,” Sadiq said.CM Omar later shared Sadiq’s statements on X.A Union home ministry protocol directive in Feb mandated the six-stanza version of the song at all state functions, official events and legislature sessions. In Aug, the President cleared Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, which puts Vande Mataram on a par with the national anthem, making disrespect/disruption a punishable offence. The amended law did not change the stanzas, but people are now obligated to respect Vande Mataram as a constitutional duty.NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar said: “This is a constitutional obligation, and every one holding a constitutional office has to accept it, whether it is the CM, an MP or anyone else,” he said, adding the full version is now regularly played at govt functions across J&K.Dar acknowledged the objection among Muslims. “Though religiously it is not acceptable to Muslims, it is a constitutional obligation that has to be fulfilled,” he said.The freedom movement broadly adopted first two stanzas of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’s 1875 poem, while the full song has six containing religious imagery that has drawn objections from Muslims. Congress general secretary GA Mir said freedom fighters had shaped the version used by the movement with inclusivity in mind.(inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Congress objected after all six stanzas of the national song was played at the inauguration of j&k’s first international film festival in srinagar. Nc countered, asking congress to look at cms of states governed by the party, including telangana and karnataka.

Article Title: ‘Wanted to teach him a lesson’: Accused on assault that killed Manipuri musician
Article Text:
Accused wanted to ‘teach him a lesson’, police say

Police examine racial angle, dhaba owner’s role

Singh died hours after assault

Northeast body seeks swift, impartial probe

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Who was Chongtham Vikram Singh?

NEW DELHI: The men accused of killing Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh in southeast Delhi allegedly wanted to “teach him a lesson” for objecting to noise outside his home, but did not expect the assault to turn fatal, police said on Wednesday.During questioning, the accused allegedly told police that they assaulted the 54-year-old musician with fists and blows after he objected to the commotion outside his residence in Kilokari, according to the police, as cited by news agency PTI.Singh had on some occasions complained to the owner of a nearby dhaba about the noise caused by people gathering there, a senior police officer said. However, police had not received any formal complaint from Singh regarding the noise.The dhaba remained open until around midnight and attracted customers from neighbouring areas as well as students living nearby, police said.Police said they were examining all aspects of the case, including whether there was any racial angle. So far, the investigation has not revealed any instance of a racial slur being used against Singh during the altercation, a police source said.The FIR registered at Sunlight Colony police station on the complaint of Singh's son mentions Section 103(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, pertaining to group murder in circumstances covered by the provision.Police are awaiting the post-mortem report to ascertain the exact nature of the injuries sustained by Singh. Prima facie, he appears to have suffered internal injuries that led to his death.The police are also examining the role of the dhaba owner and its operations. So far, no irregularity in the functioning of the establishment has come to light, sources said. Action would be taken against the owner if anything emerges during the investigation.CCTV footage is being scrutinised and witnesses are being questioned to establish the sequence of events and the circumstances that led to the assault.The incident took place around 11.30 pm on Sunday when Singh went downstairs after hearing a commotion outside his home.According to the complaint, when his son heard his father shouting, he opened the door and saw a group of men kicking and punching him.Singh subsequently returned upstairs but complained of breathlessness. His 20-year-old son Yaiphaba took him to Holy Family Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries around 6 am the following day, police said.Seven men have been arrested and a juvenile apprehended in connection with the case. The accused have been identified as Bharat Kumar, 19, Pramod, 26, Ramzan Khan, 22, Deepanshu, 21, Mohan Vishwakarma, 32, Vijay, 36, and Mannu, 26.The killing has sparked concern among members of Delhi's northeastern community, with several residents alleging that people from the region face racial slurs and discrimination in the national capital.The North Eastern Students' Organisation (NESO) on Wednesday condemned Singh's killing and demanded a swift and impartial probe.NESO chairman Samuel B Jyrwa said the incident was deeply disturbing and called for all those responsible to be brought to justice.“It is deeply disturbing that a person can lose his life merely for raising an objection to disturbance outside his own home. We demand a transparent and impartial investigation and exemplary punishment for every person found responsible,” Jyrwa said in a statement, as cited by PTI.Jyrwa said the killing could not be viewed in isolation from what he described as continuing harassment, racial discrimination, stereotyping, intimidation and violence faced by people from the Northeast in different parts of mainland India.“For years, Northeastern citizens living, studying and working outside the region have repeatedly reported being subjected to racial slurs, verbal abuse, physical attacks, social discrimination and other forms of humiliation because of their appearance, identity and place of origin,” he alleged.NESO urged authorities to treat the matter with seriousness and urgency and ensure that nobody responsible for the crime evades accountability.“The law must be applied firmly and equally, irrespective of the identity or background of the perpetrators,” Jyrwa said.The organisation also called for stronger preventive measures, effective enforcement of the law, sensitisation of police and public institutions, and mechanisms to ensure the safety and dignity of people from the Northeast.“The loss of Chongtham Vikram Singh is not merely a personal tragedy for his family and loved ones, but a matter of deep concern for the entire Northeastern community,” Jyrwa said.Singh had lived in Kilokari for more than two decades. He was a well-known musician and guitarist, and had been the lead guitarist of the Manipur rock band Phoenix in the early 1980s.He later worked as a music teacher and performer in Delhi.NESO expressed solidarity with Singh's family and the people of Manipur and demanded justice for him and accountability for everyone found responsible for his death.
Article Summary: Accused wanted to ‘teach him a lesson’, police say. Police examine racial angle, dhaba owner’s role.singh died hours after assault.northeast body seeks swift, impartial probe. Singh had lived in kilokari for more than two decades.

Article Title: 8 railway multi-tracking projects worth Rs 20,804 crore approved
Article Text:

50% Budget Spent by Sept: Vaishnaw

NEW DELHI: Govt on Wednesday approved eight railway multi-tracking projects worth Rs 20,804 crore as part of a big push for faster movement of passengers and goods across its high-density networks. PM Narendra Modi said that these projects will “ensure stronger connectivity, faster passenger movement and lower logistics cost”.Announcing the decisions, railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the multi-tracking projects -- doubling and the laying of third and fourth lines -- spanning 14 districts of West Bengal, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh; and 17 districts of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana will increase the capacity of the eight lines for running passenger and freight trains. On completion of these projects by 2029-30, the railway network will increase by 1,196 km. This is also estimated to increase freight loading by 74 million tonnes per annum.Govt said the projects are for key routes for movement of coal, cement, iron and steel, containers, automobiles, foodgrains, petroleum products and fertiliser. In a post on X, Modi said the three multitracking projects across Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal will also “encourage tourism, especially heritage and wildlife related tourism”, besides lowering logistics costs.Vaishnaw said that in the past 12 years, there has been a complete transformation of railways. The national transporter has gone for modern designs to minimise land acquisition. He added that aerial mapping and artificial intelligence–backed monitoring is helping get the actual status of land parcels. The minister also said that land related pre-investment activities are now being started before project sanction.Vaishnaw said 50% of the Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) for Indian Railways for 2026-27 has been spent till the first week of Sept. Railways have got allocation of Rs 2.8 lakh crore as GBS in FY27.
Article Summary: Govt on wednesday approved eight railway multi-tracking projects worth rs 20,804 crore. Article Title: El Nino puts India on high health-risk radar, says WHO
Article Text:
El Nino puts India on high health-risk radar, says WHO

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With dengue cases rising in several parts of the country, a WHO assessment has flagged India among nations facing high or very high health risks as a strengthening El Nino event alters weather patterns across South Asia.El Nino is a periodic warming of surface waters in central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean that can disrupt weather patterns around the world, influencing rainfall and temperatures far beyond the Pacific.WHO's Global Public Health Situation Analysis - El Nino 2026, released on Sept 5, has identified India as being at high or very high risk, with most of South Asia expected to experience drier-than-normal conditions and above-normal heat during Aug-Oct.The warning comes at a time when vector-borne diseases are already rising in parts of the country. In Delhi, 90 dengue cases were reported in Aug, the highest monthly tally this year, taking the total to 311 by Aug 29. Malaria cases also rose from 17 in July to 53 in Aug, taking the year's tally to 119, according to Municipal Corporation of Delhi.The agency does not link current dengue or malaria cases directly to El Nino, but calls it a risk modifier, with impacts depending on local weather, vulnerability and health-system capacity.For India, heat is a key concern, with higher temperatures potentially causing heat exhaustion and heatstroke and worsening cardiovascular, respiratory, kidney and metabolic illnesses.Extreme heat may also affect maternal and newborn outcomes. Other concerns include malnutrition, food insecurity and worsening non-communicable diseases. Changes in rainfall and water availability could affect food production, while heavy rain and flooding can increase the risk of leptospirosis, particularly where sanitation and drainage are poor. WHO has also flagged the India-Nepal and India-Bhutan borders, where displacement could increase the risk of cross-border disease transmission.
Article Summary: El nino puts india on high health-risk radar, says who. El nino is a periodic warming of surface waters in central and eastern tropical pacific ocean. Most of south asia expected to experience drier-than-normal conditions and above-normal heat during aug-oct.

Article Title: Pay Rs 15L to 'outstanding' officer shunted out as 'deadwood': Supreme Court
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Taking exception to Centre declaring an "outstanding" Indian Trade Service officer "dead wood" and punishing him with compulsory retirement, Supreme Court Wednesday directed all pecuniary benefits and notional promotions to him be restored and ordered govt to pay him Rs 15 lakh as compensation. S S Das was forced to retire in 2018, five years before his superannuation.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu, which had directed Centre to place dossiers and the annual confidential record of the officer before it, found he was consistently graded as outstanding/very good from 1994 and promoted just months before the punishment. It directed govt to grant Das the honourable farewell he would have been entitled to had he not been forced to retire."The manner of decision-making in course whereof 'OUTSTANDING' gradings are completely ignored, grant of promotion is looked upon as if it were a ministerial exercise, followed by a vague and omnibus finding that it is not desirable in public interest to retain the appellant in service, discloses that the officers entrusted to take a decision were determined to ensure the appellant's ouster at any cost and invented reasons to sustain a pre-decided conclusion," the bench said, calling the exercise "sheer abuse of high offices"."Having promoted the appellant, barely a couple of months later, the superior officers in the department could not have branded him... 'dead wood' to justify weeding him out. The two actions are mutually destructive and cannot co-exist," it said.SC said the action demolished the reputation of an officer which was uncalled for. It directed that Das be called to the office by the director general of foreign trade for a farewell with full honours."It must be remembered by all and sundry that reputation is not built overnight. It is built by years of dedicated and selfless service. It comes at a great cost, often at the cost of family life and personal comfort. Such a reputation earned by sweat and toil over decades can, however, be marred by a single stroke of a pen," the bench said.SC said FR 56(j) - which gives Centre the right to prematurely retire a govt servant - should not be exercised lightly or in a casual manner. "It must be founded on material which is credible, cogent and worthy of being acted up-on, and not on mere suspicion and conjecture," it added.
Article Summary: S s das was forced to retire in 2018, five years before his superannuation. Supreme court ordered govt to pay him rs 15 lakh as compensation. Justices dipankar datta and sheel nagu found he was consistently graded as outstanding/very good from 1994.

Article Title: Cyber fraud worth 5,044 crore prevented: Govt
Article Text: NEW DELHI: India is increasingly stopping cyber fraud before money leaves a victim's account. A telecom-led risk system has helped banks and payment platforms prevent suspected fraudulent transactions worth Rs 5,043.7 crore in 15 months, govt said, marking a shift from tracing stolen money to intercepting payments in real time, reports Aabhas Sharma.The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI), launched by the department of telecommunications in May 2025, assigns mobile numbers medium, high or very high risk ratings. The alerts are fed directly to banks and UPI platforms, allowing them to warn customers or block risky payments.Experts said the system's biggest achievement was making fraud operations costlier.However, fraudsters could turn to SIMs obtained through fraudulent KYC or virtual numbers. An expert said criminals could also evade mobile-number risk scores by obtaining fresh or "aged" SIM cards.
Article Summary: India is increasingly stopping cyber fraud before money leaves a victim's account. Financial fraud risk indicator assigns mobile numbers medium, high or very high risk ratings. Alerts are fed directly to banks and upi platforms, allowing them to warn customers or block risky payments.

SC reiterates call to CBSE to exempt Class VI from its 3-language policy

New Delhi:New Delhi: Supreme Court Wednesday reiterated its request to the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to consider exempting Class VI students from the three-language policy, which mandates them to take up at least two native languages, and said this would give them breathing space this academic session.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana told solicitor general Tushar Mehta that CBSE must examine extending the relaxation given up to Class VII to students of Class VI this year.Mehta said that since it has been observed by SC, he, with additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, would call a meeting of CBSE officials along with other officers concerned this week and take a call on this. "We will appraise the court of the decision taken in the next hearing," he said. SC posted the matter for hearing on Sept 17.When the counsel for petitioners referred to Justice Bagchi's earlier observation on how English should be treated - a native or foreign language - Mehta said govt has some issue with the proposition that English is a native language.Justice Bagchi said, "What is logistically less obstructive is the cutoff year for implementation of the three-language policy.Regarding the status of English, it may require full-fledged debate."SC also issued notice to CBSE on a fresh petition filed by the Forum of Minority Schools. Its counsel, Romy Chacko, told SC that it violated their fundamental rights relating to the protection of minority character of educational institutions, institutional autonomy and foundational identity, which are protected under Article 30(1) of Constitution.
Article Summary: Sc reiterates call to cbse to exempt class vi from its 3-language policy. Sc said this would give them breathing space this academic session. Forum of minority schools said it violated their fundamental rights relating to protection of minority character of educational institutions.

Article Title: Goods train derails in J&K’s Kathua, no injury or damages
Article Text:
Kathua, J&K (ANI photo)

JAMMU: A goods train derailed at Chann Aroria railway station in J&K’s Kathua district on Wednesday morning. Officials said no one was hurt and no damage was incurred in the incident.The derailment occurred around 9.30am when the goods train was heading back after unloading cement, and one of its coaches went off the track in the station’s yard, officials said. A technical team from Kathua rushed to the spot and brought the derailed coach back on track after two hours of efforts.Earlier on July 10, two bogies of a goods train moving from Jammu to Punjab derailed near Lakhanpur in Kathua after debris fell on the tracks following a rain-triggered landslide.
Article Summary: A goods train derailed at chann aroria railway station in j&k’s kathua district. Officials said no one was hurt and no damage was incurred in the incident. A technical team from kathua rushed to the spot and brought the derailed coach back on track after two hours of efforts.

Article Title: Ladakh groups claim breakthrough in talks with MHA on legislative powers
Article Text:
Ladakh groups claim breakthrough in talks with MHA on legislative powers

SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, the two organisations negotiating with the Union govt for administrative autonomy to Ladakh under the Sixth Schedule, claimed a breakthrough Wednesday in talks with the MHA’s subcommittee in Delhi on legislative powers over land, culture and language, forests and natural resources.In a joint statement, the groups said the meeting furthered the “in-principle understanding” reached during talks on May 22 and July 3 on Ladakh’s demands, including constitutional safeguards through special provisions under Article 371.They said MHA stopped short of guaranteeing powers across the board under Lists II and III of the Seventh Schedule, including law and order.MHA assured compensation to the families of those killed and the protesters injured in the Sept 24, 2025, violence in Leh, the groups claimed. The Union govt also agreed to withdraw cases against 24 people and review those against another 34 on a case-to-case basis. Cases against 25 people have already been withdrawn.Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra wrote on X about the “general air of positivity” at the Delhi meeting without elaborating beyond the agenda. “The broad contours of a sui generis model of governance under Article 371 were discussed. Deepening democracy is the goal,” he said.Another round of talks is scheduled for the first week of Oct.The groups said they were concerned over the formation of new districts, the creation of hill councils for each and what they called “major irreversible changes being done before an elected body at the Union Territory”.Making such changes before the UT body can legislate, they said, “would essentially deprive the people of Ladakh an opportunity to democratically decide on the structure of administration in Ladakh”.Ladakhi representatives have been in talks with MHA since 2023 for safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and environment. MHA set up the committee on Jan 2, 2023, but the process stalled after four people were killed and over 80 injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood in Leh in Sept last year.Activist Sonam Wangchuk , a LAB member, was accused of inciting the protesters, arrested and charged under the NSA. The Centre revoked his detention last March and he returned to the negotiating table in May.
Article Summary: Ladakh groups claim breakthrough in talks with mha on legislative powers. Leh apex body and kargil democratic alliance say meeting furthered 'in-principle understanding' union govt agreed to withdraw cases against 24 people and review those against another 34 on a case-to-case basis.
